Article Title: Rahul Gandhi stands with injured NSUI protesters, says 'nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega'
Article Text:
'Nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega': Rahul Gandhi stands with injured NSUI protesters

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress leader and Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday met NSUI protesters who alleged that they were assaulted by Delhi Police during demonstrations. At a press conference, Rahul introduced a woman protester as “our sherni” and said she had remained unafraid despite being beaten.Another protester played ‘Vaishnava Jana To’ on a flute, saying, “nafrat ka jawab pyar se diya jaega...”“I want to introduce our 'sherni'. She was beaten, but she was not afraid. There was no hatred in her heart,” Rahul said.The woman protester said that a woman police constable, identified as Chanchal Yadav, assaulted her after NSUI workers were detained in buses during a peaceful protest. She said there were around 30-40 protesters in each of the three buses, with two women and 20-30 other NSUI members in her bus.“Yesterday, all NSUI workers were protesting peacefully when we were detained in three buses. There were many of our colleagues, around 30-40 in each bus. In our bus, there were two girls and 20-30 other NSUI colleagues. There was a woman constable in the bus named Chanchal Yadav. After being detained, we tried to get off the bus again through the gate and continue leading the protest.We tried to stop the bus and sat down beneath it so that our protest could somehow continue. But Chanchal Yadav grabbed me tightly by the neck and pushed me, causing me to fall backwards onto the seat. She then scratched my face with her nails, leaving scratches across my face and near my ear. When I resisted her, she slapped me so hard and said, 'Here, take another slap across your face.'”Rahul also spoke about Athira, a student from Kerala studying at Delhi University, who alleged that she sustained injuries to her ear and eye during the police action.“Athira from Kerala has lost her hearing in one ear. She is deaf in one ear because she was struck on that ear. She can no longer hear. Last time I showed you a boy who was blinded. Now, she is deaf in one ear,” Rahul said.Athira alleged that there were no women police personnel on the bus when the protesters were detained. She said she asked for a woman officer to be present during the detention, after which the bus stopped outside the Connaught Place police station.“I am from Kerala, studying at Delhi University. Yesterday, when they detained us, there were no female police officers in the bus. So, I simply asked, 'Where is the lady police officer or lady constable?' If they want to detain us, having at least one female constable present is mandatory. Then, the bus moved and stopped in front of the Connaught Place police station, where they continuously hit my entire cheek. Because of this, I have an injury to my eye and damage to my ear. ”Rahul also condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, saying that waving the national flag during a peaceful protest was not a crime.Das and Ranka were sent to five-day judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail on Wednesday for allegedly violating their peace bonds and trespassing into Jantar Mantar, which was recently de-notified as a designated protest site, police sources said.Bail bond formalities for their associate Ajinkya Shinde were being finalised, they added.The three CJP leaders were produced before an Executive Magistrate on Wednesday morning. They had been detained on Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering the protest site without authorisation while raising slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Police registered a case against the activists on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties, sources said. Das and Ranka had signed bonds to maintain peace for a year after being detained during a protest on Saturday, they added.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi met NSUI protesters who alleged that they were assaulted by Delhi Police during demonstrations. At a press conference, Rahul introduced a woman protester as “our sherni’ and said she had remained unafraid despite being beaten. He also condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.

Article Title: 'Don't mess with youth': AAP's Sanjay Singh warns PM Modi after CJP leaders sent to jail
Article Text:
AAP’s Sanjay Singh backs CJP activists after arrest

NEW DELHI: Senior AAP leader and Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Singh on Wednesday warned Prime Minister Narendra Modi against targeting young protesters after Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were sent to five days of judicial custody following their detention in an attempt to breach Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, Sanjay accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) of opposing the national flag. He questioned the action against the CJP activists for allegedly hoisting the Tricolour and raising slogans at the protest site."Modi-ji, are you British? Is there British rule in India? I know that you people hate the Tricolour; you did not hoist the Tricolour at the RSS headquarters for 52 years. You sent CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das to jail for hoisting the Tricolour and chanting "Bharat Mata Ki Jai," he said.Warning the Prime Minister over the activists' judicial custody, Sanjay added, "Do not mess with the youth, Modi-ji; they will soon put an end to your dictatorship."CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke also criticised PM Modi, calling the action against the activists "cowardly tactics".In a post on X, Dipke said, "Ashu and Saurav have been sent to 5 days' judicial custody.Their fault? Unfurling the tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Show some guts, Narendra Modi. If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics."CJP activist Ajinkya Shinde, who was also placed under preventive arrest along with Das and Ranka, alleged that the activists were detained for waving the national flag and raising slogans of 'Vande Mataram' and 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai'.Speaking to reporters, Shinde said, "You must know that today Ashutosh, Saurav Das, and I, along with CJP volunteers, went towards Jantar Mantar, and we just waved the Indian flag and shouted Vande Mataram. So for this, this Modi-Shah fascist government has sent Saurav Das and Ashutosh to jail for 5 days," he said.The Delhi Police detained all three CJP activists on Tuesday for allegedly trespassing at Jantar Mantar while attempting to enter the site. The action came a day after authorities de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest location. Police sources said a case had been registered in connection with the incident.Earlier, CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the activists had been denied access to their lawyers for several hours and were not initially informed of the grounds for their detention. She also said the activists were likely to be produced before the relevant magistrate.The developments come amid an ongoing agitation by the CJP and Opposition parties against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
Article Summary: AAP's Sanjay Singh warns PM Narendra Modi against targeting young protesters. CJP activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das sent to five days of judicial custody. Activists detained for allegedly hoisting the Tricolour and raising slogans at protest site.

Article Title: SJM urges Centre to block Starlink’s rollout
Article Text:
Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: RSS-affiliated Swadeshi Jagran Manch (SJM) on Tuesday urged the Centre to block Starlink’s commercial rollout, questioning whether Elon Musk ’s satellite broadband service could ensure that Indian traffic passes through domestic gateways and comply with orders to restrict connectivity in specified areas.SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan said the concerns involved India’s capacity to monitor communications lawfully and enforce security restrictions. It argued that laser links between satellites could allow traffic to bypass Indian ground infrastructure and travel through foreign networks.“A key regulatory condition is that Starlink must be able to precisely restrict its services at the govt’s behest,” SJM said. It questioned whether the company could meet this requirement, citing terrorism, riots and protests as situations in which authorities may seek local shutdowns.At issue, in SJM’s argument, is whether Indian authorities can enforce security directives on a foreign operator whose network extends beyond the country’s physical borders. SJM contrasted this with incumbent telecom companies which, it said, cooperate with investigators and can suspend services in designated areas.The group accused Musk of applying public pressure instead of addressing Indian security concerns. Its intervention follows his allegation that “certain oligarchs” were blocking Starlink to protect their businesses and his criticism of Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani.SJM also flagged potential misuse by insurgents and smugglers. Starlink equipment was recovered during a drug seizure in Andaman and Nicobar Islands and an army search operation in Manipur in 2024. Musk has maintained that Starlink’s satellite beams were never activated over India.Starlink received a telecom licence on June 6, 2025, and authorisation from space regulator IN-SPACe on July 8 that year. Its commercial launch awaits completion of security assessments and spectrum assignment.On Oct 8, the communications ministry rejected the discrimination allegations as “baseless and misconceived”, saying Starlink, Jio’s satellite venture and Bharti-backed OneWeb were at broadly the same regulatory stage. Each must demonstrate security compliance before seeking spectrum, it said.Starlink has previously said Indian user data would remain within the country and its security controls would meet Indian requirements.Arguing for indigenous alternatives, SJM claimed blocking Starlink would accelerate domestic satellite broadband development and eventually deliver cheaper connectivity to remote areas. It said India’s growing space capabilities and private sector participation could support domestic alternatives, even if their rollout took some more time. It also invoked US trade restrictions, arguing India was entitled to withhold permission on national security grounds.
Article Summary: SJM national co-convener Ashwani Mahajan said the concerns involved India’s capacity to monitor communications lawfully and enforce security restrictions. It argued that laser links between satellites could allow traffic to bypass Indian ground infrastructure and travel through foreign networks.

Article Title: ‘Constitution, not convenience’: Harvard-affiliated Indians hit out at anti-EC protests
Article Text:
Harvard-affiliated Indians flag attacks on constitutional institutions and alleged misuse of the university’s name

‘Evidence, not accusations’

A group of Indian citizens affiliated with Harvard University has raised concerns over what it described as a “concerted campaign” against the country's constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, the Supreme Court, the office of the Chief Justice of India (CJI) and Parliament.In a statement issued on Wednesday, the signatories also flagged reports of Harvard University's name being used to lend credibility to a political campaign without appropriate authorisation, while calling for greater respect for constitutional values and democratic institutions."We are deeply concerned by the negative public discourse and concerted campaign against India’s constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission of India , the Supreme Court, the office of the Hon’ble Chief Justice of India, and Parliament," the statement said.The signatories expressed concern over public discourse surrounding constitutional authorities, particularly the use of terms such as “thieves” and “compromised” to describe them, and references to India being under “siege”.Such language, they said, raised serious concerns about attempts to undermine public trust in democratic institutions.“The language used to describe India as being under ‘siege’ and to characterise constitutional authorities as ‘thieves’ or ‘compromised’ raises serious concerns about the intent to undermine public trust in democratic institutions,” the statement read.The statement also addressed the role of law enforcement agencies in maintaining public order, saying their actions should be subject to fair scrutiny but that allegations must be grounded in evidence and due process.“The actions of law enforcement agencies to uphold public order deserve fair scrutiny, but sweeping accusations and abusive rhetoric cannot substitute for evidence, due process or institutional accountability,” the signatories said.They also stressed the need to respect public officials and the offices they hold, adding that constitutional principles and civil liberties must not be applied selectively.“The Constitution, rule of law, and civil liberties must be respected at all times, not just when it suits our interests,” the statement said.Summing up their appeal, the signatories said: “Our commitment must remain to the Constitution, not convenience; to justice, not selective outrage; and to democratic institutions, not the politics of accusation.”The signatories listed affiliations with several Harvard schools, including Harvard Medical School, Harvard Kennedy School, Harvard Law School, Harvard Business School, Harvard Extension School, Harvard Divinity School, Harvard TH Chan School of Public Health and Harvard Graduate School of Education.Among those named were AK Raghawan and Abhigyan Satyam of Harvard Medical School; Abhishek M, Banu Nagarajan, Bhavya Bishnoi, Deepanshu Aggarwal, Divya Dwivedi and Jaya Awasthi of Harvard Kennedy School; and Adhitya Srinivasan and Almas Lokhandwala of Harvard Law School.The statement comes as opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party have been protesting against the alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls.
Article Summary: Harvard-affiliated Indians flag attacks on constitutional institutions and alleged misuse of the university’s name. They call for greater respect for constitutional values and democratic institutions. The statement comes as opposition parties and the Cockroach Janta Party have been protesting against the alleged irregularities in the special intensive revision (SIR) of voter rolls.

Article Title: 'Declare Emergency officially': CJP's Abhijeet Dipke challenges govt after Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's arrest
Article Text:
‘Stop hiding behind police like cowards’: Dipke to PM

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday dared Prime Minister Narendra Modi to officially declare an Emergency after CJP colleagues Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail.In a video posted on X, Dipke targeted PM Modi over the duo’s judicial custody, saying Das and Ranka knew they could be jailed when they set out for Jantar Mantar but went ahead with their plan, carrying and unfurling the Tricolour.“Under Narendra Modi, even hoisting the national flag has become a violation of the law in this country,” he said.Addressing the Prime Minister directly, Dipke said, “I want to tell Narendra Modi one thing: If you have the courage, officially declare an Emergency. Stop hiding behind the police like cowards. Impose an official Emergency and say openly that dissent will not be tolerated in this country, that protests will not be allowed. Say that from now on, the only slogan permitted in this country will be ‘Har Har Modi, Ghar Ghar Modi’.He further alleged that PM Modi did not respect the national flag, the people of the country or the Constitution.“So declare an Emergency, if you have the courage,” Dipke said.Also read: CJP’s Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka arrested over trespass at Jantar Mantar; to be produced before magistrate His remarks came after Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody following an attempt to enter Jantar Mantar a day earlier. The action came after the ministry of home affairs de-notified the historic observatory as a designated protest site.Jantar Mantar, near Connaught Place and Parliament, has long been associated with demonstrations and public protests.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Wednesday dared Prime Minister Narendra Modi to officially declare an Emergency. His remarks came after CJP colleagues Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail. Dipke targeted PM Modi over the duo’s judicial custody.

Article Title: 'Murdering democracy': Opposition slams Centre for the arrest of CJP leaders
Article Text:
Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka detained over attempt to enter Jantar Mantar

Rahul Gandhi: ‘Jantar Mantar belongs to people of India’

MK Stalin offers legal support

Arvind Kejriwal questions arrests

Aaditya Thackeray says protest will continue

Abhishek Banerjee targets BJP

Mamata Banerjee condemns arrests

Mahua Moitra expresses solidarity

D Raja calls arrests undemocratic, demands immediate release

Why were the CJP leaders arrested?

NEW DELHI: Opposition leaders on Wednesday slammed the Centre over the arrest of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were sent to five days of judicial custody after protesting at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee called the situation “BJP’s new Pakistanified Bharat”, while leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said jailing young protesters for waving the Tricolour was “an act of cowardice”.Leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi said waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar during a peaceful protest was not a crime and called jailing the two men “an act of cowardice”.“Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause,” he said, adding that the groups were united in demanding their constitutional rights. “Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. We will reclaim it.”Former chief minister of Tamil Nadu and DMK president MK Stalin questioned how many protesters the government could detain and how many young voices the BJP could silence. He said jailing more young people would prompt more ordinary citizens, including those without political affiliations, to take to the streets.Stalin expressed solidarity with Das and Ranka and said the DMK was ready to provide them with all necessary legal representation and support.AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal questioned whether waving the national flag in India could be considered a crime.“Is waving our own flag in our own country a crime? This is absolutely ridiculous,” he said.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray said the two CJP leaders had been jailed for holding the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar. Asking when holding the national flag had become a crime for young Indians, he said the fight would continue until democracy was reclaimed.Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP of arresting Indians for unfurling and waving the national flag in their own country. He called the situation “BJP’s new Pakistanified Bharat”.Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee strongly condemned the arrest of CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, calling it an attempt to intimidate and silence an entire generation.“We must never surrender our constitutional rights,” she said, urging people to unite to protect democracy. Banerjee also alleged that 14,000 people in West Bengal were facing police and political atrocities, and said young people could count on her support. “Your Didi is with you — today and forever!” she said.Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra expressed solidarity with the two arrested leaders, writing: “With you boys. We will reclaim this country from these thugs & looteras.”Communist Party of India (CPI) general secretary D Raja called the detention and judicial custody of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka “undemocratic”, alleging that the case over trespassing amounted to harassment.Raja pointed out that Jantar Mantar had been a designated protest site until two days earlier and accused the government of trying to curtail protests and silence dissent out of fear of public anger. He questioned when protesting against an “undemocratic order” had become a crime and demanded the immediate release of the two leaders.Raja said the denotification of Jantar Mantar would be challenged politically and legally. He added that the All India Students’ Federation (AISF) and All India Youth Federation (AIYF) had marched to reclaim the protest site and would intensify their struggle to restore the right to protest.Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained early Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, recently denotified as a designated protest site, while raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.They were sent to five days of judicial custody on Wednesday.Police have booked them on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant. The arrests came amid protests by CJP and other organisations over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders slam the Centre over the arrest of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. The two men were sent to five days of judicial custody after protesting at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: 'Abhijieet Dipke, CJP funded by US donors': Singer Mary Millben backs PM Modi; pushes for counter-movement
Article Text:

American singer Mary Millben has alleged that US-based donors opposed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi are funding Abhijeet Dipke and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), claiming that the money is being used to support forces seeking to disrupt governance in India.In a post on X, Millben appealed to young Indians to speak out, saying, “This is not the time to be silent.” She alleged that donors in the US opposed to PM Modi were funding individuals working against the prime minister and his leadership.Millben, known for her patriotic performances, came into the spotlight in India during the country's 75th Independence Day celebrations in 2022. In 2023, she performed India's national anthem during Modi's visit to the US.In her post, Millben claimed that certain US donors follow a pattern of targeting conservative leaders globally. She alleged that they “find an US educated person from the country, radicalize them, send them back to the country, and fund them to start chaos and destruction.”She also defended Modi's political record, saying the prime minister, who has served in public life for 25 years and as prime minister for 12 years, “is not going to bow to disruptive forces from my country.”Calling for a counter-movement, Millben urged young Indians to organise and peacefully protest against what she described as the “disruptive spirit of the Cockroach Party”. She added, “There should always be a counter movement to uphold democracy and freedom,” before concluding her appeal with, “Rise up, young patriots! Rise up!”The allegations come amid questions raised by BJP leaders over the funding of CJP and its founder, Abhijeet Dipke. BJP president Nitin Nabin accused opposition leaders and the CJP of attempting to destabilise India with foreign backing, while BJP MP Nishikant Dubey questioned the sources of funding behind Dipke.Dipke has rejected allegations of foreign funding, arguing that if overseas money had entered the CJP's activities, it would amount to a failure of the Union home ministry. He also challenged Union Home Minister Amit Shah to explain how foreign funding could enter the country under his watch.
Article Summary: Singer Mary Millben alleges that US-based donors are funding Abhijeet Dipke and the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) She claims that the money is being used to support forces seeking to disrupt governance in India. Millben appealed to young Indians to speak out, saying, “This is not the time to be silent”

Article Title: 'Rahul Gandhi told us to be ready at 24 hours notice for protest: Anish Gawande slams CJP leaders' arrests
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: NCP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande sharply criticised the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, calling the preventive arrest 'bizarre'. Gawande also said Rahul Gandhi had asked the INDIA bloc to be ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests, as the bloc seeks Supreme Court intervention over the arrests and other concerns related to the Election Commission.He questioned the trespassing FIR against them and asked Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar whether he supported the action against young protesters at Jantar Mantar.“This preventive arrest is bizarre. What is the actual complaint? Trespassing, filed by the JD(U)?” Gawande said, calling it a “sad day for the JD(U) and an even sadder day for Indian democracy”.Das and Ranka were detained early Tuesday after allegedly breaching barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, recently denotified as a designated protest site, while raising slogans demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The police case includes charges of trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant.Gawande invoked Nitish Kumar’s background in student politics and the JP movement, asking whether the Bihar chief minister supported the FIR against young people who, he said, were trying to wave the national flag at Jantar Mantar.He also said the INDIA bloc had been asked by leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi to remain ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests.The bloc expects the Supreme Court to address what Gawande described as an illegal FIR, alleged police brutality and concerns over the functioning of the Election Commission, including Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The arrest follows protests by CJP and other organisations over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. On October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar designated Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as venues for demonstrations, removing Jantar Mantar from the list of approved protest sites. CJP has argued that shifting protests away from the capital’s political centre reduces the visibility of dissent.
Article Summary: CP(SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande sharply criticised the arrest of CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He questioned the trespassing FIR against them and asked Bihar chief minister Nitish Kumar whether he supported the action against young protesters. Gawande also said Rahul Gandhi had asked the INDIA bloc to be ready at 24 hours’ notice for further protests.

Article Title: CJP’s Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka arrested over trespass at Jantar Mantar; to be produced before magistrate
Article Text:
Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka detained over attempt to enter Jantar Mantar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have arrested Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) activists Saurav Das , Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others for allegedly trespassing at the Jantar Mantar protest site in New Delhi.According to police sources, the activists have been taken into preventive custody, as cited by ANI.The group's legal team head Ratna Singh said the activists would be produced before a court on Wednesday."Delhi Police arrests Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, and Ajinkya Shinde at Parliament Street Police Station in today’s Jantar Mantar case. Trespass, bond violation, obstruction of public official’s duty, etc. They’ll be produced before the SCM Court in the morning. A possibility of Judicial Custody (JC) in the Tihar Jail is possible. They were not allowed to meet their lawyers till late at night. They were brought to Parliament Street PS at 3 AM in a private van. Despite these illegal actions, their spirits are high," Singh said in a post on X."Update at 5.38 am - Just been informed that Saurav, Ashutosh, and Ajinkya are likely to be produced before the SEM at Mandir Marg Police Station within one hour.FYI, 24 hours timeline will end soon," she said in another post.Earlier, Ratna Singh accused Delhi Police of acting arbitrarily and following orders from senior officials in its handling of the CJP activists. She also said that the they were denied access to lawyers for nearly 24 hours and were not initially informed of the grounds for their detention."We are currently witnessing the Delhi Police operating according to a specific 'rulebook', one dictated by orders from above. They set the law aside to follow this rulebook. We saw how people who went to Jantar Mantar, simply to hoist the Tiranga, were detained. It has been nearly 24 hours, yet they have not been allowed to meet any lawyers, nor have they been initially informed of the grounds for their detention or arrest," she said.Singh further alleged that police personnel had denied lawyers and volunteers access to the detained party members despite repeated attempts to meet them."They denied access not only to ordinary volunteers but also to lawyers who had been present since morning. The SHOs and other officers on site kept insisting they were acting under orders from above. Who, then, is issuing these orders to the Delhi Police, orders that override the law itself?" she asked.She also criticised the police for their handling of law and order in the national capital, alleging that peaceful protesters were being stopped from holding demonstrations while criminals continued to roam freely."We see criminals roaming freely, wandering the city, assaulting people, yet peaceful protesters are being stopped. Designated protest sites are being 'de-notified,' and people visiting these public spaces are being detained without explanation and held in custody for extended periods," Singh said."The Delhi Police is being used as a puppet, and they are dealing very harshly with peaceful protesters, which is not right," she added.The development comes amid an ongoing agitation by the CJP and Opposition parties against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were detained on Tuesday by Delhi Police while attempting to enter Jantar Mantar, and a case was registered against them. The action came a day after authorities de-notified the site as a designated protest venue.Following the de-notification of Jantar Mantar, authorities designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.The ministry of home affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative locations where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests. Based on the committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar was de-notified as a designated protest venue, according to the notice.
Article Summary: CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were detained on Tuesday by Delhi Police while attempting to enter Jantar Mantar. The action came a day after authorities de-notified the site as a designated protest venue. The development comes amid an ongoing agitation by the CJP and Opposition parties.

Article Title: 'Jantar Mantar belongs to people of India, will reclaim it': Rahul Gandhi slams jail term for CJP leaders

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He said that waving the national flag during a peaceful protest is not a crime."Waving the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar in a peaceful protest is not a crime. Jailing youth for it is an act of cowardice. Students. Youth. Journalists. The INDIA bloc. Different banners, one cause. All protests are one: citizens demanding their constitutional rights. Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. We will reclaim it," Rahul Gandhi said in a post on X.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal also criticised the arrest, questioning the detention of the CJP leaders. “Is waving our own flag in our own country a crime? This is absolutely ridiculous,” he said in a post on X.Das and Ranka were sent to five-day judicial custody and lodged in Tihar Jail on Wednesday for allegedly violating their peace bonds and trespassing into Jantar Mantar, which was recently de-notified as a designated protest site, police sources said.Bail bond formalities for their associate Ajinkya Shinde were being finalised, they added.The three CJP leaders were produced before an Executive Magistrate on Wednesday morning.Earlier on Tuesday the three leaders had been detained after breaching Jantar Mantar barricades and entering the protest site without authorisation while raising slogans demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.Police registered a case against the activists on charges including trespassing, violating prohibitory orders, breaching a peace bond and obstructing a public servant from discharging official duties, sources said. Das and Ranka had signed bonds to maintain peace for a year after being detained during a protest on Saturday, they added.The action comes amid heightened security in the national capital following a series of protests by the CJP and other organisations against Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Reacting to the development, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the Central government of suppressing dissent and demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi publicly declare an Emergency if the government intended to curb protests."Ashu and Saurav have been sent to five days' judicial custody. Their fault? Unfurling the Tricolour at Jantar Mantar.""Show some guts, @narendramodi. If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics," he posted on X.On Monday authorities de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest venue on Monday. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi were named as alternative sites for protests and demonstrations.According to the order, the ministry of home affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to identify alternative locations where citizens could exercise their right to protest. Jantar Mantar was de-notified based on the committee's recommendations.
Article Summary: Congress leader and leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi condemned the five-day judicial custody of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. He said that waving the national flag during a peaceful protest is not a crime. CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke accused the Central government of suppressing dissent.

NEW DELHI: An Air India flight from Frankfurt to Delhi was diverted to Jaipur on Wednesday following a security alert triggered by a suspected hijack threat.The flight, AI-2030, landed safely and was immediately escorted to a designated isolation bay, adhering strictly to standard operating procedures for aviation security emergencies.Assistant Commissioner of Police (Malviya Nagar) Shiv Dayal said airport authorities had alerted the police about the emergency landing following the threat, news agency PTI reported.Police and security personnel were checking the aircraft in the isolation bay, he added.According to preliminary information, the pilot activated Squawk Code 7500, the internationally recognised transponder code indicating hijacking or unlawful interference, while the aircraft was in the Mumbai Flight Information Region (FIR).The aircraft was subsequently diverted to Jaipur, the source said. The number of passengers on board was not immediately known.Following the aircraft's safe landing, the pilots and passengers were deboarded in a phased manner under security supervision, according to the information available. Passengers and their baggage were undergoing security screening.Ground teams from the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), airport security agencies and local police cordoned off the isolation bay and began checking the aircraft.The National Security Guard (NSG) was also placed on standby in New Delhi, according to the information provided. Further details about the security alert and the ongoing investigation were awaited.In a similar incident in August, an Air India Express flight from Dammam, Saudi Arabia, to Delhi made an emergency landing at Ahmedabad airport after a tissue paper bearing the word “bomb” was found in the aircraft’s lavatory.All 32 passengers on board were safely deboarded at Terminal 2, according to Ahmedabad Police.
Article Summary: Air India flight from Frankfurt to Delhi diverted to Jaipur. Pilot reportedly used hijack alert code Squawk Code 7500. The number of passengers on board was not immediately known. Article Title: India reaffirms Ladakh status as China says it doesn’t recognise the UT
Article Text:

Diplomatic tensions flared again between India and China after Beijing strongly opposed India’s decision to officially map and standardise 28 places in Ladakh, including some in Aksai China, and reaffirmed that it does not recognise the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh.In a swift rebuttal, New Delhi reiterated no amount of Chinese denial can change the established fact that the Ladakh UT is an integral and inalienable part of India.According to the ministry of home affairs (MHA), which announced the standardisation in a press release on October 2, identifying the places/ geographical features formally on the Survey of India map was aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal reiterated the same, saying the MHA statement was self-explanatory.“The announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders,” he said.The Chinese foreign ministry described the Indian move as illegal saying it doesn’t change the fact that the western sector of the China-India boundary belongs to China.“China has never recognized the so-called Union Territory of Ladakh unilaterally and illegally established by India, and firmly opposes the so-called standardized names publicised by India,” said spokesperson Mao Ning.However, China itself has renamed places in Arunachal Pradesh on at least half a dozen occasions in the past 10 years, including twice in 2026, to reinforce its claim over the Indian state.The fresh cartographic tussle comes in the middle of the ongoing normalisation of the bilateral relationship after a military standoff in eastern Ladakh. The Chinese response was a throwback to its statement in 2019 – a day after India revoked the special status of J&K in 2019 – accusing New Delhi of undermining China's territorial sovereignty by unilaterally changing its domestic law and establishing Ladakh UT.“Such practice is unacceptable and will not come into force,” it had then said, warning India to exercise prudence in words and deeds on the boundary question. It was perhaps no coincidence that the military conflict in eastern Ladakh started 8 months later.Beijing maintains that it has always opposed India's inclusion of “Chinese territory in the western sector of the China-India boundary into its administrative jurisdiction”. For China, Aksai Chin in the western sector remains of critical importance as it links the politically sensitive autonomous regions of Xinjiang and Tibet.However, the border situation has remained stable since PM Narendra Modi and President Xi Jinping met in Kazan in 2024. India and China have since held 3 rounds of Special Representatives talks on the boundary question, with the last round in August resulting in 8 outcomes, including a decision to advance talks for an “early and substantial” harvest of boundary delimitation and border management.
Article Summary: Beijing strongly opposed India’s decision to officially map and standardise 28 places in Ladakh, including some in Aksai China. It reaffirmed that it does not recognise the Union Territory (UT) of Ladakh. New Delhi reiterated no amount of Chinese denial can change the established fact that the Ladakh UT is an integral and inalienable part of India.

Article Title: TOI explains: Why can’t Bengaluru protest outside Freedom Park?
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A Karnataka high court order and a police licensing regime have made Freedom Park Bengaluru’s default protest venue. But the governing police order also gives the police commissioner discretion to designate another suitable venue, meaning the legal position is more nuanced than an absolute ban on demonstrations elsewhere. Here’s everything you need to know about why Bengaluru cannot protest outside Freedom Park:Bengaluru has confined protests to Freedom Park. The practice emerged from a suo motu Karnataka High Court case initiated in 2021 over the effect of demonstrations on traffic and the rights of people not participating in them.How did the restriction begin?On March 3, 2022, a division bench of the Karnataka High Court passed an interim order directing the state government to ensure that no protests, processions and similar activities were held anywhere in Bengaluru except at Freedom Park, Gandhinagar. The court also directed that such activities be organised without adversely affecting traffic, especially during rush hours, and that action be taken where traffic was disrupted.On August 1, 2022, the High Court disposed of the case. In paragraph 4, it recorded a submission that protests, marches and dharnas would be permitted only at Freedom Park, and that the state was obliged to ensure compliance with the 2021 licensing order.In paragraph 5, the operative direction required authorities to ensure compliance with that order “in letter and spirit” and to continue action against those violating it.What does the police order say?The Licensing and Regulation of Protests, Demonstrations and Protest Marches (Bengaluru City) Order, 2021, published in the state gazette in January 2022, is the rule currently governing protests in Bengaluru. It says no protests, demonstrations, dharnas or protest marches may be held in the city without a licence under the order.Clause 4.1 identifies Freedom Park as the venue for protests in Bengaluru. However, it also says that, depending on the situation, the commissioner of police may designate any other suitable place in the city for that purpose. The licensing authority may approve the number of participants at Freedom Park based on the type of programme, duration and available capacity.So, are protests outside Freedom Park illegal?Not necessarily in every circumstance. The 2021 order does not expressly prohibit protest marches, nor does it state that Freedom Park is the only possible venue: it identifies Freedom Park while preserving the police commissioner’s discretion to designate another suitable location.A legal backgrounder prepared by activists argues that the High Court’s final order did not itself direct that protests be held only at Freedom Park; it directed compliance with the licensing order. On that reading, the court’s judgment does not prevent rallies and does not mandate Freedom Park as the sole venue.The distinction matters because the March 2022 interim order did expressly restrict protests and processions to Freedom Park, while the August 2022 final order required enforcement of the 2021 licensing rules. The two must be read alongside the licensing order before drawing a definitive legal conclusion.Why does this matter?Activists argue that concentrating demonstrations at one venue reduces their visibility and makes it harder for groups to draw public attention to local grievances. The backgrounder says the restrictions have affected workers, farmers, Dalit activists, sanitation workers and residents seeking to protest on issues in their own localities.The debate is ultimately about balancing traffic management and public convenience with the constitutional right to assemble peacefully and express dissent. For now, Freedom Park remains Bengaluru’s designated and practically dominant protest venue. Whether the police commissioner’s discretion to permit demonstrations elsewhere is exercised, and on what terms, remains central to the controversy.
Article Summary: A Karnataka high court order and a police licensing regime have made Freedom Park Bengaluru’s default protest venue. But the governing police order also gives the police commissioner discretion to designate another suitable venue. The practice emerged from a suo motu Karnataka High Court case initiated in 2021.

NEW DELHI: Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Tuesday denied that Rahul Gandhi pushed him during an opposition march in Delhi, saying the Congress leader had instead expressed concern for his safety amid the crowd. The remarks come as the BJP intensified its attack over a viral video of the incident.Earlier, Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma shared the footage on X, describing the episode as “public humiliation” and questioning whether Shivakumar would accept such treatment from the Congress leadership.“Rahul Gandhi did not push me during the protest held in Delhi. He showed concern for me by suggesting that I board the vehicle following behind, as the crowd of protesters was large,” Shivakumar told news agency PTI.“No one pushed me during the protest,” he asserted, taking a swipe at the BJP for spreading what he called misinformation, while suggesting that the party had “immense affection” for him.The remarks came as Sarma drew parallels with his own fallout with the Congress before joining the BJP, recalling that he had refused to accept what he considered humiliation.“In 2015, I refused to swallow humiliation, as a proud Assamese. God was kind to me,” Sarma wrote, asking whether Shivakumar would respond similarly.“The chief minister of Karnataka is not just an individual. He is a constitutional office, and the face of a State with a glorious history, a rich culture and deep pride,” he said, adding, “Will he bow to this public humiliation?”The video, recorded during Monday’s ‘March for Democracy’ towards the Supreme Court, purportedly shows Shivakumar moving towards the front of the procession, where Rahul Gandhi was walking alongside Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and AISA chief Neha Bora.Gandhi appears to pull Shivakumar back by the collar of his kurta, after which security personnel move the Karnataka chief minister further back amid the crowd.The Karnataka BJP accused Gandhi of insulting a leader representing seven crore Kannadigas. State BJP president B Y Vijayendra termed the episode a display of arrogance and questioned the respect accorded to Shivakumar by the Congress leadership.Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya also described the alleged incident as an “insult to the dignity of 7 crore Kannadigas”.Karnataka deputy chief minister G Parameshwara, however, said crowd management during protests was difficult and that security personnel were primarily responsible for protecting Rahul Gandhi. Shivakumar had moved towards that area and was “slightly pushed” amid the crowd, he said.The march was organised by opposition leaders and civil society representatives seeking to raise concerns over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The delegation later sought a meeting with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who declined to meet it.

Article Title: ‘EC should regain credibility’: Ashok Lavasa says poll panel must regain public trust amid SIR controversy
Article Text:

Prakash Raj joins criticism of SIR

NEW DELHI: Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa on Tuesday said the Election Commission of India (ECI) was facing an unprecedented level of controversy and urged the poll body to regain public trust amid protests over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Drawing a parallel with cricket, Lavasa said the credibility of an election depended on people believing that the poll panel was impartial.“If people feel that the umpire is not neutral, they will question the winning team's victory as well,” he said while addressing a citizens' convention in Kolkata virtually, according to news agency PTI.Lavasa's remarks came as opposition parties intensified their protests against alleged “vote chori”, demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR exercise.Opposition leaders have taken to the streets in recent days and clashed with police in New Delhi.“The EC should regain its credibility and people's trust. The Election Commission of India, whose position is very high and possibly the highest among all public institutions, is today mired in controversies and people are taking to the streets to protest,” Lavasa said.The former election commissioner referred to an Indian Express report that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders they said had been issued without their knowledge.The objections reportedly came even as the nationwide SIR exercise was being overseen by the full commission.Lavasa questioned the lack of publicly available meeting minutes, saying it was difficult to establish whether decisions had been taken unanimously or by a majority.“This casts a doubt in the minds of the people whether the decisions of the Election Commission, including on the SIR, were unanimous or taken by majority,” he said.He also said the Election Commission had not provided an authentic clarification on the reported differences between its members.“Some press statements have been issued, but those create more questions and generate more doubts than they answer,” Lavasa said.The poll panel has maintained that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations in any institution. It has also said that all its orders carry full legal sanction and follow established statutory procedures.The EC added that all three commissioners, as well as its officers, were authorised to offer suggestions to improve the electoral system.Lavasa said the SIR exercise had triggered widespread anxiety over voting rights, adding that people had not been as concerned about protecting their right to vote in the preceding 16 months.“The EC's decision to conduct the SIR took everyone by surprise,” he said.He noted that the Election Commission had conducted special revisions of electoral rolls in the past under the Representation of the People Act and the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, but argued that the current exercise had created an unprecedented level of public concern.Lavasa also questioned the approach of categorising electors into three age groups based on their dates of birth under the Citizenship Act.The Constitution, he said, requires the Election Commission to enrol all those who meet the eligibility criteria under Article 326, which provides for voting rights for Indian citizens aged 18 and above who are not of unsound mind or disqualified under any law.“But unfortunately, with the tactics deployed this time, the goal is not to include. Possibly the priority is to exclude people from the voter list on the suspicion that they are not Indian citizens and not on evidence,” he said.Referring to West Bengal, Lavasa said nearly 60 lakh people's voting rights had gone under adjudication during the SIR, apart from those excluded from the draft electoral rolls. He said the EC had not adequately considered the proximity of the Assembly elections and the difficulty of adjudicating such a large number of cases in time.Lavasa added that around 33 lakh names had been restored to the voter list after adjudication.Actor-activist Prakash Raj, who also addressed the convention, described the SIR as the “most dangerous disease” and alleged that it was undermining democracy.“Even before Gyanesh Kumar came (as the CEC), they broke parties in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, and Bihar,” he said, accusing the BJP leadership of seeking to divide people through the SIR into those who could vote and those who could not.Raj also alleged that the West Bengal Assembly elections were conducted in an “illegal” manner following the revision exercise, claiming that voter names had been selectively deleted. He said opposition parties had come to believe they were contesting “fixed” elections.The convention was organised by CPI(M) leader Bikash Ranjan Bhattacharya and retired bureaucrat Jawhar Sircar.The protests over the SIR have also prompted a wider political confrontation between the opposition and the ruling BJP.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has vowed to continue the INDIA bloc's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities, while Union home minister Amit Shah has accused the Congress of trying to shield infiltrators by opposing the exercise.
Article Summary: Former election commissioner Ashok Lavasa says the Election Commission of India is facing an unprecedented level of controversy. Lavasa urges the poll body to regain public trust amid protests over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Opposition parties have intensified their protests against alleged “vote chori”

Article Title: 'Lady hiding in Dehradun': Who was Rahul Gandhi referring to at INDIA bloc presser?

Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge, party leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal, and other leaders of the INDIA bloc address a joint press conference, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

Why is Seema Khanna's name in the controversy?

NEW DELHI: “It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," Rahul Gandhi said announcing a united INDIA bloc's resolve to continue its agitation against alleged SIR irregularities.A day after the INDIA bloc's high-voltage protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi hosted a high tea for opposition leaders at his residence. Following the meeting, INDIA bloc leaders addressed a press conference."Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India," Rahul said.But then who was the 'lady hiding right now in Dehradun' whom the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha was referring to in his statement?Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders have been relentless in their attacks on the Prime Minister and the Union home minister, but it was his reference to a 'lady hiding in Dehradun' that added an element of mystery to the press conference.Was the Congress leader referring to Seema Khanna, the Election Commission's Director General (IT), whose name has figured in opposition allegations of 'vote theft'?There is no confirmation that Khanna is the woman Rahul was referring to. The Congress leader did not identify her, and there is no independently verified information linking her to Dehradun. However, her name has repeatedly surfaced in allegations raised by opposition leaders against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Khanna's name came into focus following a report by The Indian Express, which said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Among the concerns raised was the growing centralisation of control over electoral-roll software and restrictions on the powers of Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), who are legally responsible for maintaining voter lists.The controversy centred on the Election Commission's digital systems, including ERONet and ECINet, which are used to manage electoral rolls and election-related services. ECINet is a unified digital platform developed by the Election Commission to streamline electoral processes and improve transparency and accessibility.The investigation raised questions about whether local election officials had adequate access to make corrections, restore voters' names and exercise their statutory powers, or whether some of these functions had become concentrated within the Commission's IT department headed by Khanna.Rahul Gandhi did not name Seema Khanna, but AICC media coordinator Harmeet Kaur appeared to draw a connection between his remark and the EC official in a post on X."Where is Seema Khanna? Is she hiding in Dehradun? And who is shielding her? Remember EC data still under her control! Who is protecting her, and what are they trying to hide?" Kaur wrote, sharing a video of Rahul's remarks at the press conference.Last month, Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra filed a police complaint against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station, alleging procedural violations, unilateral decision-making and manipulation of electoral rolls.Speaking to ANI, Moitra directly named Khanna while accusing the Election Commission of manipulating voter lists through its software."Very important things like the crores of new voters were not being allowed to come on the list because of the addition of a new question on Form 6, the new voters list. And we now find that the two other election commissioners had said this is completely illegal; still, the question linking parentage was put in," Mahua Moitra had said."We find how the EROs and the BLOs and the ground-level officials were not kept in the loop and denied access to the software, and Seema Khanna, who was DGIT, along with Gyanesh Kumar, played with the software from the back end to manipulate voter lists while keeping EROs and block-level officials in the dark. This is a very serious charge," she alleged.She also questioned changes to Form 6, used for registering new voters, and alleged that 33 lakh valid voters in West Bengal had been kept off the electoral rolls through questionable appeals.Moitra argued that decisions taken without the consent of the other two Election Commissioners could not be treated as decisions of the full Commission. These allegations have not been established.The Election Commission, however, has maintained that differing views among its commissioners are part of the decision-making process and that its decisions were unanimous. It has also described ECINet as a unified platform intended to improve electoral services.While Khanna's name has repeatedly figured in the wider controversy, there is still no confirmation that she was the woman Rahul Gandhi referred to during Tuesday's press conference.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi's reference to a 'lady hiding in Dehradun' adds an element of mystery to the press conference. Was the Congress leader referring to Seema Khanna, the Election Commission's Director General (IT), whose name has figured in opposition allegations of 'vote theft'?

NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for Information and Broadcasting L Murugan has sought to step down from the Union Council of Ministers and relinquish his Rajya Sabha membership, saying he wants to return to grassroots politics.Murugan said he intends to devote himself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu and preparing the party for the 2029 Lok Sabha elections.In a letter addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Murugan said he wished to focus on expanding the party’s presence across the state. He also shared the letter on X, reiterating his commitment to working with party workers.“With humility and a grateful heart, I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibilities as Minister of State and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha, so that I may dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu,” Murugan wrote in the letter.He added, “I want to go to every village and every street, meet our people, stand beside our karyakartas and help expand the party's presence in every part of the State.”In his post on X, Murugan said, “It has been the greatest honour of my life to serve Bharat Mata and Tamil Nadu under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi.”“Now, I wish to return to the grassroots, stand with our karyakartas and dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the BJP in Tamil Nadu ahead of the 2029 Lok Sabha elections,” he added.Murugan also expressed gratitude to Modi for giving him the opportunity to serve in the Union government, highlighting his background as the son of daily wage labourers.“I do not come from a political family. I come from a very poor family. My parents, who worked as daily wage labourers and cattle grazers, continue to lead a simple life in Konur village,” he wrote.Reflecting on his political journey, Murugan said his guiding principle over nearly three decades in the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and the BJP had remained: “Nation First, Party Next, Self Last.”Murugan has served as minister of state for Information and Broadcasting and Parliamentary Affairs. Article Title: Sunak meets Modi, hails his leadership as UK-India ties go ‘from strength to strength’

Former UK prime minister Rishi Sunak met Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Tuesday and congratulated him on completing 25 years in public service. Praising PM Modi’s commitment and work ethic, Sunak said the UK-India relationship was going from “strength to strength” under his leadership.In a post on X, Sunak recalled working with PM Modi during his tenure as prime minister and highlighted the importance of closer cooperation between the two countries in trade, technology and artificial intelligence (AI).“Prime Minister Narendra Modi great to see you in New Delhi today. Congratulations on 25 years in public service, a remarkable achievement. It was a pleasure to work with you when I was Prime Minister,” Sunak wrote.Praising Modi’s approach to public service, he added, “Your commitment, your work ethic, your energy is an example to us all.”On bilateral ties, Sunak said, “The UK India relationship is going from strength to strength under your leadership. Our two countries cooperating more on trade, tech and AI is vital in a less predictable world.”He also expressed confidence in the future of the partnership, writing, “I know that Britain and India will continue to grow ever closer in the years ahead.”Earlier on Tuesday, Sunak spoke about the changing global order and the growing ability of countries such as India and those in the Gulf to pursue independent foreign policy positions amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty.Speaking at a panel discussion titled “The End of Predictability” at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026 in New Delhi, Sunak said the world was moving away from the multilateral, rules-based framework that had shaped the global economy.“We all grew up investing in, operating in a multilateral rules-based framework, largely enforced by US President Trump is not a cause for that; he's a symptom of that, and the world that we're in now is one where we don't quite know what we've settled down to, and that creates an enormous amount of geopolitical uncertainty and indeed danger,” he said.Sunak also described China’s emergence as a strategic competitor to the United States as a significant shift.“So, China is a peer competitor for the US across economic, military, and technological domains. The co-architect of Vote Chori has, not surprisingly, ‘predicted’ the 2029 Lok Sabha election for which undoubtedly he has already begun the rigging process. But it is not going to happen. NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi 's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. They met for a high tea after four days of protest and filing a petition in SC against the CEC.From directly slamming the CEC to criticising the SIR process and criticising PM Modi and Amit Shah, several leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting.Here's what some of the key leaders saidLeader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi anonunced that the INDIA bloc would continue its fight to restore the democratic process and ensure accountability for those he accused of undermining it. "We are all standing here together as one. As I said yesterday, there are no parallel protests. There is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: restoration of democracy in India.Democracy has been destroyed in this country. The election system has been destroyed. The Constitution has been torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule, genuine democratic rule in this country."He thanked people who supported the protest and vowed to bring those responsible to justice. "It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice.""Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India. This is about the future of the people of India, and we, all of us together, because we love you and we respect you, are going to fight to the end to restore the democratic process in this country. It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," he added.Further assuring the work of the team, the Congress leader said, "I used the word 'perseverance' at the press conference yesterday—that this team of ours is not going to stop. Sooner or later—whether tomorrow, the day after, in three months, six months, a year, or two years—it will not stop. It will reach the end goal. I cannot tell you exactly how we will get there, because that would spoil the surprise, and we want to maintain the excitement and sense of surprise for you and the country. But I guarantee you that just as we mobilized—with such energy, strength, and unity—we will continue to fight together in the same spirit. Thank you to the Supreme Court—we have immense respect for the Supreme Court, the Chief Justice of India, and the Indian judicial system; they have a role to play, and we hope they will play it. However, we are political people; no matter what happens, or which institution plays a role or doesn't, political resistance will continue, people's resistance will continue, and it will triumph."The Congress president hailed INDIA bloc protests against "vote chori", CEC as "massive success". "We will carry forward this united fight (protests) against Modi govt, "vote chori", he said.Giving highlights of what they decided in the meeting, he said, "We held a meeting with senior leaders of the INDIA bloc, where we discussed the current situation in the country and how to take forward the campaign demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar."Further slamming the decision to de ntoify Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he added, "The government has now denotified Jantar Mantar. We strongly condemn this decision. Jantar Mantar must remain a place where people can protest.""Gyanesh Kumar has joined the ruling party's team... He steals votes, protest site and democracy," said CPI(M) leader M A Baby after the INDIA bloc meeting ."(CEC) Gyanesh Kumar is a "mafia" who has criminalised entire system; we know how to fight such mafia," he said. Further talking about the meeting, he added, "Rahul ji had convened it and invited everyone—leaders and MPs were present for the high tea—and it was a very good meeting. Discussions were held, and everyone's suggestions regarding the way forward and their respective views were taken into account; however, the ongoing struggle against CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Modi ji, and Shah ji will continue—both in the national capital and elsewhere. "She accused the Election Commission of undermining free and fair elections. She demanded a halt to the SIR process, restoration of previous electoral rolls, Kumar’s removal and criminal proceedings against officials allegedly involved in electoral irregularities."Every day, it is becoming increasingly clear that the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission is undermining free and fair elections in India. As long as the Gyanesh Kumar-led Election Commission continues to function, there will be no free and fair elections in India. We stand completely united with all the leaders and parties of the INDIA alliance. We will not stop until Mr Gyanesh Kumar is removed and criminal proceedings are initiated not only against him but also against all Election Commission officials who supervised elections in Haryana, Maharashtra, Bengal and Bihar, because these have been elections marked by vote chori," she said."The government currently in power in Bengal is illegitimate. It came to power through vote chori...We have a set of demands: halt the SIR process, stop it and revert to the old electoral rolls. Gyanesh Kumar must be dismissed, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against him. All officials, who have been involved in vote chori, must be investigated, and criminal proceedings must be initiated against them. We will not rest until this Election Commission is held accountable," she added.Sule expressed solidarity against the CEC and stated that their agitation will continue. "We stand united with full strength as part of the INDIA alliance; our struggle will continue because the Constitution has been undermined and is currently in danger in this country. We will persist with our agitation to uphold the rights granted to all Indians in the Constitution by Bharat Ratna Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar. A single individual—representing a single government—is making a grave mistake by attempting to trample upon these rights. We stand united with full strength to fight against this injustice and oppression; our movement will continue, from Delhi down to the grassroots level," she said.Taking aim at the govt said, "Govt's vote chori exposed before people. We are all together and will win." Criticising the move to remove Jantar Mantar as a protest site, he added, "Govt's fear is evident in denotification of Jantar Mantar as protest site."She directly took at aim at the BJP and said, "The one enemy of the people of this country, of Indian democracy, and of the Constitution is the BJP.An attack on voter rights is an attack on India and an attack on democracy.CEC Gyanesh Kumar must go.The SIR process is compromised."
Article Summary: India bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. Leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting.

Article Title: Protest fundamental to democracy: Karnataka Govt; Then don’t cage us in Freedom Park: Activists
Article Text:

BENGALURU: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge and chief minister DK Shivakumar Tuesday reiterated that peaceful protest is fundamental to democracy and promised a review of police action against anti-SIR demonstrators in Bengaluru.Activists, however, said assurances were not enough and demanded the withdrawal of the police licensing order restricting protests to Freedom Park and restoration of the 2009 order governing assemblies and processions.The demand follows Monday’s detention of protesters who had gathered near KR Circle to march to the chief electoral officer’s office against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Police detained them after they refused to move to Freedom Park, while photojournalists covering the action were also allegedly manhandled.Kharge said he had instructed police to ensure peaceful demonstrations were not disrupted. Shivakumar said he had sought a full report on the circumstances leading to the police action and warned that accountability would follow if there had been unnecessary use of force or excess.“The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy. We cannot demand that right for ourselves in Delhi and deny it to others in Bengaluru,” Shivakumar said, adding that there would be “no double standards”. He, along with Kharge, was in Delhi on Monday to protest against SIR.Activists welcomed the assurances but said the govt must address the restrictions that, they argue, make it difficult to protest at the site of an issue or draw public attention to local grievances.“The Licensing Order, 2021 by the commissioner of police restricting protests to Freedom Park must be withdrawn, just as any restriction to designated venues for protests in any city. Protests cannot be caged in Freedom Park; holding placards and shouting slogans cannot be criminalised; peaceful marches cannot be met with police violence,” advocate and activist Clifton Rozario said.He added that police power could not be used against legitimate struggles in defence of the Constitution.My Vote, My Right, which had organised Monday’s protest march, welcomed Kharge’s decision to review the police handling of protesters and journalists, but urged the govt to withdraw the 2021 licensing order and restore the “2009 assemblies order”. The organisation also questioned Shivakumar over what it saw as a contradiction between his participation in a protest in Delhi and the action against demonstrators in Bengaluru, asking: “One law for you, one law for us — why?”A woman protester who was forcibly dragged away by police on Monday said restricting demonstrations to Freedom Park curtailed citizens’ rights. “This rule is what allows the police to deem any protest outside the said venue, even if it is barely a kilometre away, illegitimate,” she said.Activists under the Horatada Hakkigagi Janandolana said the restriction had also affected people seeking to raise local issues. A protest over a neighbourhood grievance, they argued, loses its immediate relevance when residents must travel to a central venue to be heard. They have cited workers, farmers, pourakarmikas, Dalit activists and residents protesting civic issues among those whose demonstrations have been affected.The coalition was, as of late Tuesday, preparing a fresh memorandum to the govt. On the same as the CM and Kharge’s assurances, Bengaluru police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh said KR Circle was a heavily congested junction and police had asked protesters to shift to Freedom Park. He said the protesters refused and blocked the road, following which police removed the blockade and made preventive arrests.Acknowledging a confrontation involving protesters, police and media personnel, Singh described it as unintentional and said officers had been instructed to exercise utmost care. He maintained that the right to protest in Bengaluru was, under the court’s order, limited to Freedom Park, and said police were prepared to provide protection when informed in advance.Activists insist that reviewing Monday’s police action must go hand in hand with changing the rules governing where people can demonstrate. They want the govt to withdraw the 2021 order and restore the 2009 framework, under which they say protests could be held at different locations after informing the police.
Article Summary: Karnataka home minister Priyank Kharge and chief minister DK Shivakumar Tuesday reiterated that peaceful protest is fundamental to democracy. They promised a review of police action against anti-SIR demonstrators in Bengaluru. Activists, however, said assurances were not enough and demanded the withdrawal of the police licensing order restricting protests to Freedom Park.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said he had spoken with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, with the two leaders agreeing to build on the positive momentum in India-Canada ties and work towards concrete outcomes across key areas of their strategic partnership.In a post on X, PM Modi described the conversation as “warm and productive” and said the two sides would focus on trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties.“Together, India and Canada are contributing towards a more stable and prosperous world,” PM Modi wrote.The conversation comes amid efforts by the two countries to strengthen ties and advance negotiations for a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA), which both sides hope to conclude by December.India and Canada are currently in the fifth round of negotiations for the proposed trade agreement.
