He last visited Canada in June 2025 to attend the G7 Summit at Carney's invitation.Alongside trade, New Delhi and Ottawa have been seeking to deepen cooperation on security and defence.During the latest round of bilateral security dialogue, both sides welcomed efforts to advance CEPA negotiations and underlined the potential for a more substantive defence relationship.National security adviser Ajit Doval and his Canadian counterpart, David Morrison, also reviewed progress in security and law enforcement cooperation under a shared Security Work Plan concluded in February.In a joint statement, the two sides said they would explore further practical cooperation, including structured dialogues on cyber security and economic security.They also agreed to strengthen coordination against transnational organised crime, terrorism, violent extremism, human and drug trafficking, cybercrime and extortion, as well as on the extradition of criminal offenders.PM Modi and Carney had previously discussed bilateral relations during meetings in New Delhi in March and on the sidelines of the G7 Summit in Évian in June.

NEW DELHI: External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Tuesday said that if China wants a normal relationship with New Delhi, the border between the two countries has to be stable.During a conversation at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum, Jaishankar said that India and China do not have an agreed border and that the issue has persisted for decades."We don't have an agreed border between India and China. This is not a new issue; it's been going on for multiple decades... From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said."Then in 2020, when we were in the midst of the Covid lockdown, we had a series of border issues, and it culminated in a clash in which a number of soldiers were killed on either side," Jaishankar added.Jaishankar said that if peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences."For us, what it represented was a very profound departure from the situation that was prevailing since 1975. If the peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences. Those consequences were very visible for the next five years until we were able to restore the peace and tranquillity.It took four years of negotiations," he added."The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense. It's a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable, that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas.' As the border areas are settling down, they have settled down to a great extent since 2024; the relationship is commensurately moving towards normalcy," he further said.This comes after the ministry of external affairs reiterated that the Union territory of Ladakh is an integral and inalienable part of India after the Chinese foreign ministry opposed the naming of certain strategic locations in Ladakh."The announcement mentions that the twenty-eight (28) places/features located in the UT of Ladakh have been identified with standard place and feature names on the official map of Survey of India, and it has been done in consultation with the Union Territory of Ladakh and local stakeholders," MEA said."Identifying these places formally on the Survey of India map of UT of Ladakh is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the public at large," the ministry said.On October 2, India formally identified 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh on its official map, including key border friction points along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), such as Gogra and Hot Spring.The move, undertaken in consultation with the Ladakh administration, aimed to improve official mapping, ensure precise identification and raise public awareness of the sensitive border region.
Article Summary: External affairs minister S Jaishankar said that if China wants a normal relationship with New Delhi, the border between the two countries has to be stable. India formally identified 28 strategic locations and geographical features in Ladakh on its official map, including key border friction points.

Article Title: Over half of Amaha clients live with mental health concerns for a year before seeking help; 56% report self-harm thoughts
Article Text:
Many people struggle with mental health issues for over a year before seeking professional help

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Mental health concerns can persist for months, sometimes years, before people seek professional help. By then, the distress may be affecting their relationships, work and ability to manage everyday tasks. More than half of people who eventually sought care had lived with their concerns for over a year, while 56.2% reported thoughts of self-harm before reaching professional support, according to the Amaha Mental Health Report 2026.The report is based on responses from 13,825 people who answered questions before beginning care with the mental healthcare provider between October 2025 and September 2026. Only 11.3% sought help within a month of experiencing mental health concerns.Dr Amit Malik, psychiatrist, founder and CEO of Amaha, said, “India’s progress in mental health must be judged by whether people can get timely, effective care, not simply by how openly we talk about it. These are the accounts of people who reached us; they should make us ask who is still unable to access care.”He added that friends, families and communities were vital to helping people recognise their needs and find care, and said finding treatment should not become “another test of a person’s resilience”.Nearly 95% of respondents reported at least two concerns, averaging five each. Anxiety was most common (72.1%), followed by stress (67.5%), low mood (58.3%), relationship difficulties (55.6%) and sleep disturbances in over a third. The report also found a gap between self-reported distress and clinical diagnosis: 33% of those initially reporting stress were later diagnosed with depression, while among those reporting repetitive thoughts and behaviours, 32% were diagnosed with depression and 11% with obsessive-compulsive disorder.Before approaching a professional, many respondents relied on informal support or tried to manage their concerns on their own. More than half (54.5%) had spoken to friends or family, while 44.6% had turned to self-help resources such as books, apps, videos and online communities. Nearly a third had tried therapy previously, and 19.4% had used prescribed medication.Avoidant coping strategies, including excessive screen time, oversleeping and overworking, were reported by 82.7%. Another 15.4% said they had turned to alcohol or other harmful substances instead of professional support.The impact extended to everyday functioning. Only 12.3% said they could manage all their daily tasks, while 27.3% said they could not manage most tasks or any at all.Young adults and working professionals formed the bulk of the cohort. Those aged 25–34 accounted for 51.3% of respondents, followed by 26.9% aged 18–24. Working professionals made up 64.3%, while students accounted for 15.3% and unemployed people 7.9%.Friends were the most frequently named contact in a mental health crisis (33.9%), followed by spouses (20.5%) and siblings (18.1%), underscoring the role of family and social networks in recognising distress and helping people access care.
Article Summary: Mental health concerns can persist for months, sometimes years, before people seek professional help. More than half of people who eventually sought care had lived with their concerns for over a year. Only 11.3% sought help within a month of experiencing mental health concerns.

A Saudi national and OpenAI engineer has been arrested by US federal agents and charged with allegedly installing a hidden audio recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company to capture sensitive discussions about its technology, the US Justice Department said Tuesday.The employee, identified as 35-year-old Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested on Friday.The complaint did not name the company, but OpenAI confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices”. The company reported the discovery to the FBI and fired the employee.“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson was quoted as saying by AP.“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement read.The complaint does not specify what Alfozan intended to do with the recorded conversations. However, OpenAI said the device was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and equipped with advanced encryption and audio-monitoring capabilities.The company also said it had evidence that the employee planned to install additional listening devices in other parts of the office building to record meetings.Alfozan appeared in court for the first time on Tuesday. He faces a charge of using or attempting to use an electronic, mechanical or other device to intercept oral communications.According to the complaint, the recording device was found on September 30, concealed in toilet paper and plugged into a USB port at the back of a television in an executive conference room.The conference room did not have a security camera when the device was installed. However, CCTV footage from other parts of the office showed Alfozan near the room on nearly a dozen occasions last month, despite having no authority to access the space or attend meetings there, the complaint said.OpenAI later installed a camera in the room. According to the FBI, footage recorded last week showed Alfozan entering the room and checking behind the television where the device had been placed.The complaint also alleges that Alfozan used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, room capacities and calendars.Days before his arrest last week, Alfozan allegedly left an unattended bag in another room. When OpenAI personnel opened it, they found his wallet, identification documents and another recording device similar to the one discovered in the executive conference room, the complaint said.
Article Summary: Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, arrested over hidden recording device in executive conference room. OpenAI confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices” The company reported the discovery to the FBI and fired the employee.

NEW DELHI: US secretary of state Marco Rubio will visit Mumbai and Jamnagar from October 17 to 22 as part of a trip to India and Uzbekistan, with talks in India set to focus on strengthening bilateral strategic ties and expanding energy cooperation.According to a media note issued by the US department of state, Rubio will travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan before arriving in India for his second official visit to the country this year.During his India visit, Rubio is set to meet senior government officials to strengthen the US-India strategic partnership, exchange views on regional and global developments, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. NEW DELHI: Union minister L Murugan on Tuesday offered to resign from the Cabinet and Rajya Sabha, saying he wanted to return to politics in his home state, Tamil Nadu, after being part of govt for over five years. This rekindled the buzz that PM Modi could be preparing to reshuffle his council of ministers amid a steady exit of its members and some being in the queue.Murugan has three and a half years left of his RS term, and his exit will allow BJP to pick a new face from Madhya Pradesh, where he was elected from in 2024.In his five-page letter, Murugan expressed gratitude to the PM for all the opportunities he got and his govt's work for Tamil Nadu. He said, "I therefore request you to relieve me of my responsibilities as Minister of State and permit me to relinquish my membership of the Rajya Sabha so that I may dedicate myself full-time to strengthening the party in Tamil Nadu."What stoked curiosity in political circles is that he chose to post the letter offering his resignation on social media, apparently with the consent of the BJP leadership. This suggested a clear signal from the party brass, leaving many within the governing alliance wondering if it was a prelude to more resignations.L Murugan's exit comes on heels of BJP not renominating ministers Hardeep Puri and B L Verma for another term in RS. Ravneet Bittu and George Kurian have already resigned earlier under similar circumstances.Two other ministers, Pankaj Chaudhary and Harsh Malhotra, have been made chiefs of BJP units in UP and Delhi, making their departure only a matter of time.Interestingly, an imminent RS vacancy from MP opens up the possibility for Puri, the lone Sikh face in the govt, to return to Rajya Sabha.Murugan has been BJP chief in Tamil Nadu, the last one among big states where BJP remains on the margins of electoral politics, and it was given a jolt when K Annamalai, who enjoyed a decent following, quit in June 2026.

Article Title: Sensex jumps 1100 after finance minister's remarks spark LTCG cut hopes

NEW DELHI/MUMBAI: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman Tuesday said the govt was open and keen to "hear" discussions around the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax as it was "healthy" to have the debate.The minister, however, declined to be specific on the matter as preparations for the Union Budget in Feb are already underway.The FM's comments raised investors' hopes of a reduction in LTCG tax and securities transaction tax (STT), a longstanding demand among foreign funds who have been big sellers in the Indian market in the last two years.As a result, after a steady start, stock prices jumped with the sensex finally settling 1.5% or 1,109 points up at 73,034 points while Nifty closed 1.6% or 359 points up at 22,722 points.While responding to an observation that investors, especially foreign funds, were keen on removal of capital gains tax and streamlining of taxation before they started investing in India, Sitharaman said, "Two years ago, we had bought all the asset classes similarly and people thought that I was increasing the tax. I was not increasing the tax, I was bringing all of them at par, so that an investor is not speculating as to which one gives them greater leverage.So, these are the things on which there is a lot of debate. It's healthy to have this debate and I will be keen to hear them."At a Bloomberg event, FM acknowledged that investors, both within and outside, were commenting on LTCG and the question of treating all asset classes similarly has been a widely discussed topic.So far this year, foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have bet sold Indian stocks worth a little over Rs 3 lakh crore, NSDL data showed. In 2025, the corresponding figure was a net outflow of nearly Rs 1.7 lakh crore and just Rs 427 crore in 2024. Since Sept 2024, sensex has lost about 13%.At the same event, Sitharaman also noted that rupee has depreciated "significantly" over the past year and a half, and RBI will continue its efforts to prevent excessive volatility. "RBI is not trying to fix the rupee, it is trying to stop the volatility, and for that there is a lot of effort from their side. I am sure RBI will take further steps to make sure that rupee does not become too volatile," she said in response to a query on capital outflows, especially in the equity market due to currency depreciation.FM stressed that govt has kept the economy on a sound footing and been careful with its spending and borrowings, helping investors looking to diversify away from China. "Fiscal discipline is not going to be a matter which should worry investors," she said, adding that domestic private capital is moving in and is attracting private capital from elsewhere as well.At a time when foreign funds are taking money out of India at a fast clip, a relook at the taxes related to the markets is a welcome move.According to Hitesh Sawhney, partner at Price Waterhouse, against the current backdrop of sustained foreign investor selling, elevated global yields and capital moving towards competing markets, revisiting LTCG taxation may be timely."A (zero) tax rate on LTCG, linked to a relatively longer holding period, could reward patient capital, encourage investors to remain invested in India and strengthen India's relative capital market attractiveness. It would also reduce foreign investors' dependence on treaty-based exemptions and the resulting uncertainty over treaty eligibility."
Article Summary: Nirmala Sitharaman says govt is open and keen to "hear" discussions around the long-term capital gains (LTCG) tax. FM's comments raised investors' hopes of a reduction in LTCG tax and securities transaction tax (STT)

NEW DELHI: Taking cognisance of allegations that women journalists were sexually harassed by police personnel while covering the Oct 10 protest for resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Supreme Court Tuesday asked Delhi Police to depute a senior officer to the court on Thursday to respond to the charges.Senior advocate Indira Jaising said that 'Network of Women in Media' has filed a petition narrating the incidents of sexual harassment of women reporters during the anti-SIR protest on Saturday.When Jaising said she has already served an advance copy of the petition to solicitor general Tushar Mehta, who is representing Delhi Police, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "We would like some senior police officer to remain present in the court to explain and assist the court."The day also saw senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia and Mahesh Jethmalani mentioning a petition seeking initiation of criminal contempt action against political leaders for storming SC on Monday evening and obstructing access to SC's petition filing counter, thus blocking the access to justice. The reference was clearly to leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc members who were part of a procession to SC on Monday.Bhatia and Jethmalani sought a ban on political activity inside the court's premises and preservation of CCTV footage of Monday evening.During an extraordinary hearing on Sunday - on the Oct 10 protest - SC had found authorities to have prima facie breached its Oct 9 order restraining complete closure of metro stations and train services in the capital on the day of protest.It had sought responses from Union home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and Delhi Metro chief on contempt petitions filed against them. The bench also accepted the solicitor general's request for extension of time till Thursday for home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and Delhi Metro chief to file their responses.Senior advocate Nithya Ramakrishnan, appearing for Apoorvanand Jha, alleged that students who were detained by police on Oct 10 were tortured in police custody.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi peddling lies on SIR to cover Congress poll defeats: Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Going on the offensive amid opposition's stir against special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Union home minister Amit Shah Tuesday accused Rahul Gandhi of fabricating lies about the exercise to hide his failure resulting in a string of Congress defeats, and to protect "infiltrators" who have been registered as voters."You and not SIR is responsible for Congress's defeats. Since you emerged as the main leader of Congress and then became its president and the leader of opposition, Congress has continuously lost elections. You should introspect," he said, asking the main opposition party and its allies to prepare themselves for a fourth consecutive defeat in the 2029 Lok Sabha polls."In many states you have not been able to win election for decades," Shah said, citing Congress's barren electoral performance in a number of states, including in Gujarat, Tripura, Tamil Nadu and West Bengal, while SIR had started only after 2024.This is the first time Shah has taken on the opposition, which has been trying to ratchet up pressure for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation through its street campaigns in the national capital, and signalled a determined intent of the BJP brass to challenge its opponents' allegation that Election Commission (EC) is working to benefit the party in polls.The framing of opposition's protests as an attempt to cover "infiltrators" is significant, as BJP has for long accused its opponents of helping illegal immigrants from Bangladesh as well as Rohingya from Myanmar getting registered as voters as part of their "votebank" politics.With opposition parties coming together, BJP and JD(U) held a joint press conference where Union minister Piyush Goyal dared opposition-run govts in different states to quit if it considered polls following SIR rigged.Union minister and JD(U) functionary Lalan Singh said the entire campaign is not for saving democracy but weakening it by targeting constitutional institutions and trying to stoke anarchy through street protests. The two ministers echoed Shah on Congress's poor show in UP, Bihar and Tamil Nadu for decades, and said it is not even a key party in vast swathes of the country.Union home minister Amit Shah's sharp comments came after BJP notched up another facile win in three local body polls in Gujarat, leaving Congress far behind. Aam Aadmi Party lost deposits in all 32 seats it contested in Gandhinagar Municipal Corporation, he noted.This win coupled with BJP and its allies' similar impressive show in local body polls in Tripura and Rajasthan, besides in the recent assembly and LS bypolls, demonstrated that people of the country are standing with PM Modi, BJP, and NDA like a rock, Shah said.Many of these polls were held through ballot papers, he said, as the opposition has often blamed EVMs for its losses. "These elections are a lesson for Rahul Gandhi... You (Rahul) cannot win the confidence of people by fabricated media events, 'jhooth ki goonj'," Shah said, riffing on Rahul's "Chhatron ki Goonj" outreach to students in different cities.Mocking the opposition's march in New Delhi on Monday, he said Rahul Gandhi cannot become the voice of the people by mobilising cadres of 14 parties to collect a crowd of 8,000 through a distance of 1.5km. They have no reach in the vast hinterland, he added. "Your negative politics will not benefit you. You should connect with people," he added.
Article Summary: Union home minister Amit Shah accused Rahul Gandhi of fabricating lies about the exercise to hide his failure resulting in a string of Congress defeats. This is the first time Shah has taken on the opposition, which has been trying to ratchet up pressure for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.

Article Title: SC bar association to file contempt plea against Kerala Congress for CJI post
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) Tuesday decided to file a petition seeking initiation of contempt proceedings against Kerala Congress for its social media post (which was later deleted) asking CJI Surya Kant to quit for iterating the constitutional mandate that law and order does not lie in the domain of judiciary.SCBA chief Pradeep Rai said the process of drafting the plea is continuing and would be sent to attorney general R Venkataramani seeking his consent for its filing in court.Contemporaneously, Mamata TMC MP Mahua Moitra sarcastically misspelt the CJI's name and posted on X, "Surya clearly can't, So we will." It immediately drew an official response from Mamata TMC, distancing itself from her post.SCBA and SCAORA condemned Kerala Congress. SC Women Lawyers Association, led by advocate Mahalakshmi Pavani, said, "Any deliberate attempt to demean, discredit or undermine the institution, or to erode public confidence in it through irresponsible, intemperate or unwarranted remarks, is a matter of concern.""The freedom to express disagreement does not absolve anyone of the responsibility to exercise restraint, fairness and respect when speaking about constitutional offices and institutions," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) to file a petition seeking initiation of contempt proceedings against Kerala Congress. Kerala Congress MP Mahua Moitra sarcastically misspelt the CJI's name and posted on X, "Surya clearly can't, So we will"
